investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Agent Provisioning Evals (production-api)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-23T12:26:08–12:26:41Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api layer could not reach the swarm backend ELB at /v1/agents during agent provisioning. Because the failure occurs at the very first HTTP call to POST /api/agents, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected, and the expected-output contract is entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB-backed backend reachable at the redacted us-east-2 endpoint — was unreachable from the production-api layer at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check depends on a successful POST to /api/agents, which proxies to http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents. That upstream call failed with code bad_gateway across all three checks, preventing agent creation from starting and leaving all required evidence fields empty. This is an eval-observed infrastructure connectivity failure localized to the swarm gateway dependency; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: POST /api/agents failed with 502 bad_gateway — 'swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning: error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)'
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical 502 bad_gateway message, latencyMs=10961, endedAt=2026-08-23T12:26:30.242Z
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical 502 bad_gateway message, latencyMs=10857, endedAt=2026-08-23T12:26:41.099Z
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent — consistent with the request never completing
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}), confirming no agent was provisioned
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=11168 — well under the warningLatencyMs=240000 threshold, indicating a fast upstream rejection rather than a timeout

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after requireOrgId — the 502 would surface at this createAgent call before any evidence is written
source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:179-187: all three failing checks belong to the same remote-agents feature and share the same swarm-backed provisioning path
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The swarm gateway ELB in us-east-2 was down, misconfigured, or had no healthy targets at the time of the eval run — all three checks hit the same 502 from the same upstream endpoint within a ~33-second window.

[Possible] A network routing or security-group change between the production-api layer and the swarm ELB caused connectivity to drop, producing a bad_gateway at the API gateway layer before the ELB could respond.
[Possible] The swarm service behind the ELB crashed or was restarting, causing the ELB to return 502 because no backend instances were healthy.
[Less likely] A transient network blip in us-east-2 affected only the swarm ELB path; the failure may have self-resolved by the time a re-run is attempted.

[Cannot assess without additional evidence] A deployment or configuration change to the swarm service or its ELB listener coincided with the eval window — sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges is empty, so no specific change is implicated.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful POST /api/agents response (2xx) at or near the eval timestamp would indicate the swarm gateway was reachable and the failure was isolated to the eval runner's network path or credentials.
ELB access logs showing no 502s for /v1/agents around 2026-08-23T12:26:08–12:26:41Z would suggest the failure occurred between the production-api layer and the ELB rather than at the ELB itself.
A passing re-run of the remote-agent-create eval immediately after the incident with no infrastructure changes would suggest a transient network blip rather than a sustained gateway outage.

If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state or remote-agent-runtime passed, the shared-dependency hypothesis would be weakened and the failure would be localized to the create path specifically.

Evidence that the eval runner's access token was invalid or expired (causing the API to return 502 instead of 401) would shift the root cause to an auth/credential issue rather than a gateway connectivity issue.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated swarm-gateway-health eval that directly probes the ELB health endpoint (if one exists) before attempting agent creation, so gateway-level failures are distinguished from agent-creation-logic failures.

Add a pre-flight connectivity check eval for the swarm ELB that runs before remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime, allowing downstream check failures to be attributed to the shared dependency automatically.
Add a historical baseline eval that tracks consecutive failure counts for the remote-agents feature and pages when the swarm gateway has been unreachable for more than one eval cycle.

Consider adding a remoteGatewayReachable evidence key to the remote-agent-create contract so that gateway connectivity failures are surfaced as a distinct evidence gap rather than a generic 502 message.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Agent Provisioning Evals (production-api)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-23T12:26:19–12:26:41Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway ELB endpoint was unreachable during agent provisioning. Because the eval runner's remote-agent-state probe calls createAgent as its first substantive step (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905), the 502 from POST /api/agents → http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents aborted execution before any required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) could be collected.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning endpoint — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check depends on a successful POST /api/agents call to create a remote agent before any further state or runtime probing can occur. The gateway returned a 502 bad_gateway with error code "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning" for all three sibling checks, producing zero evidence output and causing the remote-agent-state contract validation to fail on all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state). This is an eval-infrastructure signal of a backend dependency outage localized to the swarm gateway / remote agent provisioning path; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production user impact.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Agent Provisioning Evals (production-api)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-23T12:26:08–12:26:41Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api layer could not reach the swarm backend ELB at /v1/agents during agent provisioning. Because the failure occurs at the very first HTTP call to POST /api/agents, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected, and the expected-output contract is entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB-backed backend reachable at the redacted us-east-2 endpoint — was unreachable from the production-api layer at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check depends on a successful POST to /api/agents, which proxies to http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents. That upstream call failed with code bad_gateway across all three checks, preventing agent creation from starting and leaving all required evidence fields empty. This is an eval-observed infrastructure connectivity failure localized to the swarm gateway dependency; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:179-187: all three failing checks belong to the same remote-agents feature and share the same swarm-backed provisioning path
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The swarm gateway ELB in us-east-2 was down, misconfigured, or had no healthy targets at the time of the eval run — all three checks hit the same 502 from the same upstream endpoint within a ~33-second window.

[Possible] A network routing or security-group change between the production-api layer and the swarm ELB caused connectivity to drop, producing a bad_gateway at the API gateway layer before the ELB could respond.
[Possible] The swarm service behind the ELB crashed or was restarting, causing the ELB to return 502 because no backend instances were healthy.
[Less likely] A transient network blip in us-east-2 affected only the swarm ELB path; the failure may have self-resolved by the time a re-run is attempted.

[Cannot assess without additional evidence] A deployment or configuration change to the swarm service or its ELB listener coincided with the eval window — sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges is empty, so no specific change is implicated.

recommendedNextActions: Check the health of the swarm gateway ELB in us-east-2 (target group healthy instance count, recent scaling events, listener rule changes) around 2026-08-23T12:26 UTC to determine if the gateway was down or had no healthy targets.
Re-run the three remote-agents eval checks immediately to determine if the failure is ongoing or was transient — a pass would indicate recovery, a continued 502 requires gateway-level intervention.

Review AWS ELB and swarm gateway service logs for the /v1/agents path around 2026-08-23T12:26 UTC to identify the specific cause of the 502 (no healthy targets, connection timeout, upstream crash, etc.).
If the gateway is confirmed down, escalate to the team responsible for the swarm infrastructure in us-east-2 to restore ELB target health.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: The error message names an AWS ELB in us-east-2 as the unreachable endpoint. Checking target group health, recent deregistrations, and listener rules around 2026-08-23T12:26 UTC would confirm whether the ELB had healthy backends at the time of failure.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful POST /api/agents response (2xx) from the same production-api environment at or near the same time window would indicate the gateway was reachable and the failure was isolated to the eval runner's network path or credentials.
If re-running the eval immediately returns passing results with all five required evidence fields present, the failure was transient and the gateway has recovered — not a sustained outage.
If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create or remote-agent-state passed, the root cause would be localized to the runtime check's logic rather than the shared provisioning gateway.

AWS ELB access logs showing successful /v1/agents requests from the production-api source IP during the 12:26 UTC window would suggest the 502 originated from application-layer logic rather than ELB unreachability.
Evidence that the eval runner's access token or network egress was misconfigured (e.g., token expired, wrong VPC routing) would shift the cause away from the gateway itself.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated swarm-gateway-health eval that directly probes the ELB health check endpoint (independent of agent creation) so gateway unreachability is detected before the full agent provisioning flow is attempted.

Add a gateway-connectivity pre-flight check that runs before remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime — if the gateway is unreachable, skip downstream checks with a clear 'gateway unreachable' status rather than failing all three with the same 502 message.
Add historical run tracking for remote-agent-runtime (currently previousRunCount=0, lastPassingAt=null) so future regressions can be detected against a known-good baseline.
Consider a retry-with-backoff eval variant for the remote-agent-runtime check to distinguish transient network blips from sustained gateway outages before recording a hard failure.
